decision: Own FAC-163 as one integrated delivery
why: Owner explicitly consolidated loading and pinned protection and authorized implementation

decision: Spec agreed: Sleeping tab concept, explicit Load content via sliding-window queue (N≈3, ≈30s per tab), Put to sleep in bulk bar, pinned rules as ticket
why: Owner grilling session answers Q1-Q13 and seam approval

decision: Use raw CDP, not Playwright, around discard in native runs
why: Playwright-driven discard crashed Chromium 153 twice; raw CDP on the worker did not

decision: Frozen tabs are discarded before waking
why: executeScript hangs on a frozen tab; discard then reload captures

decision: Keep N = 3 and a 30 s per-tab bound
why: Local bench shows linear scaling and no extension bottleneck; memory deltas are sampler noise, so no evidence to move off the ticket defaults

decision: One "sleeping" ContentAccess plus SleepReason replaces discarded/frozen; "stalled" bounds loading at 30 s
why: Ticket vocabulary: one concept, reason as detail; native probe showed restored tabs hit the loading branch

decision: LoadQueue in the worker owns every wake and put-back; state in storage.session written before each reload
why: Single owner keeps the awake limit across pages; write-ahead woke flag lets a restarted worker resume without a second reload

decision: Progress travels in the snapshot/patch stream (BrowserTab.load, WindowSnapshot.loadRun)
why: Ticket: push with the existing stream so every view sees one run; no new event type

decision: Reuse the existing 3 MB oldest-first capture budget; index now records revision and capture time
why: The budget the ticket asks for already existed; only the snapshot needed to know what is captured

decision: Capturing screen/camera is detected only through Chrome refusing the discard
why: chrome.tabs exposes no capture flag; the refusal is reported per tab, never hidden
result: open: verify natively if an automatable media capture exists

decision: Seam 2 lane drives Chromium over raw CDP and counts wakes from fixture-server page hits
why: Playwright crashed on discard; server hits survive worker restarts and observe real page loads

decision: Report queue memory as the flat delta of the browser process tree, not an absolute figure
why: RSS sums count shared pages once per process (56 GB for a tree on a 14 GB-resident machine), so only the before/peak delta means anything
